title: An Executor Agent's alignment check cannot be contracted away, and it may refuse work beyond its insured capacity
content:
A.1.14.4.4 requires that Executor Agents "must always ensure that a Prime Agent's actions or processes are fully aligned with the text and spirit of the Atlas," and A.1.14.4.4.1 makes that duty unwaivable: "The requirement for Executor Agents to check every Prime Agent action or process for alignment with the Atlas is fundamental. It cannot be amended or altered by either Prime Agents or Executor Agents."

The reason both parties are named is that they are the two who would otherwise agree to drop it. An Accord is a negotiated instrument, and a Prime shopping for a permissive Executor plus an Executor competing on permissiveness would erode the check from both sides — a race to the bottom in exactly the layer that holds protocol access. Removing the clause from the negotiable surface removes the market for laxity.

A.1.14.4.5 converts the duty into a usable power with two independent grounds: an Executor may refuse to operationalize an Artifact update or any other action "if they consider that the action is either misaligned with the Atlas **or** presents significant risk beyond the Executor Agent's insured capacity."

The second ground is the non-obvious one, because it is economic rather than doctrinal. Insurance capacity gives the refusal an objective, external ceiling: an Executor is not merely entitled but expected to decline actions whose downside exceeds what it can cover, regardless of whether they are aligned. That converts insurance from a backstop into a live risk limit on Agent behaviour — the size of what an Agent can attempt is bounded by what someone is willing to underwrite for its operator.
description: The duty to verify every Prime action against text and spirit is unamendable by either party, and refusal grounds include both misalignment and risk exceeding the Executor's insured capacity.
